hook: A brain receptor needs a second, always-on receptor to signal and ease psychosis-like signs in mice.
hook_turn: and ease psychosis-like signs in mice.
summary: Mouse hippocampal neurons let the mGlu2 receptor trigger calcium signals only when the platelet-activating factor receptor, which is constitutively active, is also present. Blocking that partner receptor weakened the signal, and the partnership was needed for mGlu2 drugs to rescue cognition and behavior in a mouse model of NMDA receptor hypofunction. The evidence is from mice and cultured neurons, so human benefit is untested.
title: Synergy between Gq and Gi proteins for the antipsychotic-like effects of mGlu2 receptors.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
